LeaveType.title: Leave type
LeaveType.description: A kind of leave an employer offers, administered rather than enumerated: a code, a label, whether it draws from a balance, whether it needs a reason or a document, and how far ahead it may be requested. Adding zorgverlof is writing an object, not changing a schema and shipping a release (leave-against-a-department-schedule, REQ-LVM-T01). A LeaveRequest carries the code of its type, so a request written before this schema existed still resolves to the type whose code it already holds.

code.title: Code
code.description: The short code a leave request carries, for example holiday or zorgverlof.
code.x-notes: Stable identifier. LeaveRequest.leaveType holds this value, which is why a code is never rewritten once requests carry it.

label.title: Label
label.description: What this kind of leave is called on screen.

drawsFromBalance.title: Draws from the balance
drawsFromBalance.description: Whether approving this kind of leave draws hours from the employee's balance.
drawsFromBalance.x-notes: False means the approval posts nothing to LeaveBalance: unpaid leave and most bijzonder verlof draw down no entitlement.

requiresReason.title: Needs a reason
requiresReason.description: Whether a request of this kind can only be submitted with a reason filled in.

requiresDocument.title: Needs a document
requiresDocument.description: Whether a request of this kind can only be submitted with a document attached.

maxNoticeDays.title: Maximum notice in days
maxNoticeDays.description: How many days ahead this kind of leave may be requested at most. Leave empty for no limit.
maxNoticeDays.x-notes: Checked on submit only: a request starting further ahead than this is refused, naming the condition. Calamiteitenverlof is the case this exists for.

active.title: Active
active.description: Whether this kind of leave is offered on new requests. A retired type still resolves on the requests that already carry it.
